subject: Computer Networking
title: HTML — The Web's Language
description: A quick win: understand HTML — The Web's Language.

hook.text: Every web page is an HTML document. Tags define headings, paragraphs, links, images, and structure.

buildup.text: HTML uses nested tags: <html> wraps <head> and <body>. The browser reads this tree and renders a page.

discovery.text: Semantic tags like <article>, <nav>, and <footer> give meaning. Screen readers and search engines rely on them.

twist.text: HTML alone is ugly. It provides structure, not style. CSS adds the colors, layout, and typography.

climax.text: HTML5 added video, audio, and canvas natively. Plugins like Flash became obsolete overnight.

punchline.text: HTML is the skeleton of every web page. Structure first, style later.

quiz.question: What did HTML5 make obsolete for playing video on the web?

details.summary: HTML is the markup language that structures web content using nested elements defined by tags. Headings, paragraphs, links, images, and forms are all built with HTML elements. Semantic HTML communicates the meaning of content to browsers, search engines, and assistive technologies.
details.whyItMatters: HTML is the foundation of every web page. Writing semantic HTML improves accessibility, SEO, and maintainability — it tells machines what content means, not just how it looks.
takeaways: HTML structures content with nested elements defined by tags
Semantic elements like article, nav, and aside convey meaning
The DOM tree representation enables JavaScript interaction

faq.question: What is semantic HTML?
faq.answer: Semantic HTML uses elements that describe content meaning rather than appearance. A nav element indicates navigation, article wraps a self-contained composition, and aside marks supplementary content. This helps search engines understand page structure and screen readers navigate content.

faq.question: How does a browser process HTML?
faq.answer: The browser parses HTML into a Document Object Model tree, where each element becomes a node. It then applies CSS styles to calculate layout and paints pixels to the screen. JavaScript can modify the DOM dynamically. This parse-style-layout-paint pipeline runs for every page load.
